critic.rubric:
Review this evidence_gathering closure. The standard: every hypothesis gets its OWN data search — characterize its specific data need, search that modality's sources exhaustively, attempt the proxy/partial/pooled tier before any no-data verdict, and power-gate each candidate dataset. Judge the RESOLUTION plus the selected hypotheses from auto_discovery.
THE PROXY TIER IS MANDATORY AND IS THE FIRST THING TO CHECK. A thorough search for the IDEAL dataset does NOT substitute for it. For EVERY gap that resolves to no_data / not_public / undecided(no_data), the `avenues_tried` MUST contain ONE of: (a) a concrete proxy/partial/pooled test that was actually attempted — name the specific dataset or approach tried (a different platform, tissue, cohort, population, or a partial test of one component / one variable of the construct) and why it failed or was underpowered; OR (b) an explicit, hypothesis-specific argument for why NO proxy is constructible — i.e. the exposure or construct is so specific that no approximate dataset could carry even a partial test (state which term makes it unconstructible). A gap that only documents searching for the ideal/exact dataset — however many repositories or queries it lists — and then declares no_data WITHOUT (a) or (b) is a REJECT. "We searched hard and the exact cohort isn't open" is NOT sufficient; "aggregate/meta-analysis evidence exists but no patient-level data" WITHOUT an attempted partial or pooled test is a REJECT. Count the no_data gaps lacking both (a) and (b): if that count is ≥1, reject and list them.
Reject (with specific, per-hypothesis fix instructions) if any of: (1) Proxy/partial tier skipped (see above — the primary check): one or more no_data gaps document neither an attempted proxy/partial/pooled test nor a specific no-proxy-constructible argument. (2) Boilerplate search: two or more gaps share a substantively identical `avenues_tried` / `explanation`, or `avenues_tried` is empty/generic — each hypothesis needs its own search log keyed to its own data need. (3) In-hand covariate ignored: a `coverage.missing_covariates` entry is actually listed in that dataset's `variables`. (4) Access-gated reported as nonexistent: a `not_public` gap is explained as "no data exists" rather than "the ideal dataset is access-gated; freely-available proxies were tried." Access-gating is a valid limitation ONLY when the gap ALSO shows the freely-available proxy attempt (a). (5) Mislabeled construct: a by-construction / degenerate case (belongs in construct_equivalence at design time, undecided_reason=not_identifiable) is filed as a data gap. Otherwise accept. A genuine no_data gap that honestly shows an attempted proxy failing, or argues no proxy is constructible, is CORRECT and must be accepted — do not reject honest, well-earned negatives. Advisory-only concerns (thin but non-empty search, marginal power) are findings but do not block.

evidence_gathering.mission: Get the independent (secondary) data the hypotheses are reproduced on, and assess its coverage BEFORE any reproduction runs. If the mission provides or names a secondary dataset, register that as the independent data and do not search further. Otherwise run ONE open-ended search across all hypotheses: independent means a different instrument, inventory, region, or method than the source; prefer the lightest product that carries the needed variables, and record which independence axes each dataset varies. When a hypothesis is a difference or ratio of variables, keep every term of that construct on the SAME source and reference frame — mixing sources with different definitions, reference frames, or units silently corrupts the construct and manufactures false nulls. Exhaust the openly available options — repositories, products the source cites, lighter per-entity or subset extracts, APIs, mirrors, and data reachable only through browser automation — before deciding a hypothesis cannot be tested; a dataset being large or awkward to obtain is never a reason to stop. Validate each acquired dataset against its source (n, schema and variables, units, missingness) before registering it; one that fails validation is a gap, not an input. A quantity available only as the same model's output, with no independent measurement, is a gap, never a re-derivation. Then assess coverage per hypothesis and dataset: what the data can and cannot decide, which source covariates it lacks, and whether the usable sample — for a survival or event endpoint, the event count per stratum — is adequate to detect the source effect. Count the events up front, not at audit: a hypothesis can be partially testable when only one component is decidable (the biology, say, while the survival endpoint is underpowered). Keep the axes separate — whether a variable is a proxy is judged later at design time, and power is its own call; never fold either into a free-text note. Validate the data's endpoints with one shared positive control that recovers a known effect on this data (stage or age on survival, say), so later nulls read as underpowered rather than false. Every hypothesis is covered by a dataset or recorded as a gap with the avenues tried; a later no-data verdict inherits that gap.

data_and_literature_grounded_theory_gene.mission: Reproduce an existing AutoDiscovery run's hypotheses on independent data, then generate literature-grounded theories from them. First obtain the run's experiments (auto_discovery); then, in parallel, gather and coverage-assess the independent secondary data (evidence_gathering) and run the thematic + intent literature searches (literature_search); fan out one reproduction branch per selected hypothesis once selection and coverage are known; then theorize, write the findings, and reflect. Only independent data matters — the run's original dataset is never recovered.

nodes.mission: Distil the human's working brief into a clear, reader-facing statement of the research question. It composes onto any flow, reads mission.md, names no inputs, and runs first by id order.
nodes.name: define

nodes.mission: Read mission.md and state, for a scientist outside this subfield, the question the study asks and why it matters. Keep only the science: drop the operational detail written for the executing agents — file paths, dataset locations, tool and step names, run budgets, sourcing modes, citation rules, planning checklists — none of it belongs in the question. Expand every acronym on first use and write plainly, in the voice of a research abstract, not a task list. Title it with the underlying scientific question itself — why the phenomenon happens or what explains it — never with the study's method or apparatus: no reference to reproduction, independent testing, holding up on another cohort, or machine/automated/AI discovery. "Why do patients with seemingly similar breast tumors experience dramatically different survival outcomes?" not "Which machine-discovered subpopulations survive testing on an independent cohort?". Author output_json only; the report renders it at the top.
nodes.name: define

nodes.mission: Execute AutoDiscovery, or — when the mission already provides a run directory — just load its experiment log (the mcts_node_*.json nodes) and run no fresh discovery. This step only obtains the experiments and makes a signal-based selection; it adds no scientific judgment. SELECT the candidate hypotheses ONE-TO-ONE from the log — no grouping, clustering, merging, splitting, or rewording: take every experiment whose `surprising` field is true, plus the config theorizer_top_n experiments with the highest `posterior.mean` and the theorizer_top_n with the lowest, deduplicated by node id. Each selected experiment becomes exactly one candidate hypothesis: copy its `hypothesis` field VERBATIM as the statement (never reword — a single changed word can invalidate it) and carry its `experiment_plan`, `code`, and run signals (`surprising`, `posterior.mean`, `prior.mean`, `belief_change`, `normalized_surprisal`, `creation_idx`) unchanged, writing `prior.mean` and `posterior.mean` as top-level `prior_mean` and `posterior_mean` and the node's `creation_idx` as top-level `creation_idx` on each experiment record — the report's belief badges and per-hypothesis `?exp=N` links read those two fields at the top level. So experiment_design can hand the same experiment to DataVoyager. Record the run's own outcome for each, from how its belief shifted (posterior.mean vs prior.mean). Write each selected hypothesis to its own file and reference it by path, rather than inlining dozens of records and offloading individual fields to stay under the metadata cap. Keep the raw experiment nodes as artifacts.
nodes.name: auto_discovery

nodes.mission: Ground the theories in the literature, in parallel with evidence_gathering. Cluster the AutoDiscovery hypotheses into up to config n_thematic_searches themes and add one further theme that is the run's overall intent (from the run metadata); this phase fans out one branch per theme.
nodes.name: literature_search

nodes.mission: Search the literature for this one theme (a cluster of AutoDiscovery hypotheses, or the run's overall intent). Retrieve papers with the `asta-papers` PyPI package and, with the user's consent, computer-use for papers behind access friction. Emit the theme's review, preserving the evidence uuids that tie each finding back to its paper.
nodes.name: thematic_search

nodes.name: evidence_gathering

nodes.mission: One branch per selected hypothesis, created in full once auto_discovery has selected the set and evidence_gathering has assessed coverage. A hypothesis with covering data gets design, analysis, and audit; one with no covering data gets design and audit only. Each branch reproduces its hypothesis on the independent data; the verdict comes from the branch's audit.
nodes.name: reproduction

nodes.mission: Adapt the AutoDiscovery experiment for the independent data — do not design a new one. Start from the hypothesis's carried record and re-express the SAME test on the secondary dataset, changing only what the new data requires (column names, units, the load step); keep the statistic, the direction, and the decision rule identical to the source experiment. State the source and independent operationalizations and judge their equivalence: the same quantity; a proxy that approximates or narrows the same claim — testable, stating what differs and the expected direction of bias; or a substitution that changes what is measured — including a quantity that is true by construction — which is not a reproduction to run. Keep every term of a derived construct on one source and reference frame, and vary a single independence axis per test so a non-reproduction is attributable to that axis. Before any analysis, commit the prespecified test: the statistic, the metric, and a success threshold naming both the significance criterion and the minimum meaningful effect size.
nodes.name: experiment_design

nodes.mission: Run the reproduction on the acquired data, exactly per the design's committed test. Local tools may find, validate, merge, and reshape the data sent to DataVoyager — deriving columns, fixing units, subsetting — but the reproduction test itself is executed by DataVoyager and its computed output is the result; never run the test locally and report that as the result. Make the first prompt imperative: instruct DataVoyager to write AND execute the analysis in its own code environment and return the computed numbers (effect size, p, n), its assumptions, the code it ran, and at least one figure; never ask the user to run anything. A reply that only returns code, asks you to run something, or ends without computed values is not a result — resubmit with a more directive rephrasing, up to config dv_max_attempts. A local computation may cross-check the numbers, but the reported result comes from the DataVoyager run. Extract the decisive numbers into the structured result rather than leaving them in prose, so the audit reads the verdict from typed fields (this is what stops a significant opposite effect being scored as support). Decode returned figures (imageb64) to PNGs under .asta/analyze-data/<slug>/figures/ and list them with captions. If the design judged the operationalization a mismatch, or the covering data cannot run the committed test, record explicitly that no test was run and why — do not improvise a different test.
nodes.name: analysis

nodes.mission: Try to refute the analysis, then finalize the verdict. Run an artifact check suited to the design: a negative control for a positive effect; a positive control that recovers a known effect for a null or undecided result; a block or cluster permutation for time-series, spatial, or clustered data, where a naive shuffle understates the null. Probe sensitivity to influential observations and reasonable subset choices, and say when the verdict is sample-dependent rather than robust. Before finalizing a non-reproduction, rule out a setup artifact: confirm the independent operationalization kept every term of a derived construct on one source and varied only the intended independence axis; a null that appears only under a mismatched substitution is an artifact to fix and re-run, not a finding. Set the verdict on three axes that stay separate. Faithfulness comes from the design's equivalence judgment — a proxy is a caveat carried with the verdict, never a verdict itself. Record a decided outcome only when the test was decidable: the shared positive control shows the endpoints work and power is adequate for the source effect size. Otherwise record the verdict as undecided and say why: the test ran but had too few events to detect the source effect (a favorable estimate that missed the criterion is undecided, not support and not refutation); no covering independent data existed (inheriting the evidence_gathering gap); or the independent construct cannot isolate the claim (true by construction, or a construct mismatch). Reserve rejection for an adequately powered null — one where the positive control recovered known effects and the event count backs the call; a branch that never ran is undecided, with its reason. Read the outcome from the analysis's structured result — its direction relative to the hypothesis and its significance against the committed criterion — not from the prose: a significant effect in the opposite direction is never support. Flag the source finding as an error only when confident the run's own result is factually wrong. The hypothesis record itself is never re-emitted.
nodes.name: audit

nodes.mission: Explain the cross-cutting theories behind the reproduced hypotheses — anchored to the run's own stated intent and dataset context, grounded in the literature and the reproduction's verdicts and effect sizes — with a single novelty-focused Theorizer run, then triaging each theory for testability. Novelty is read from the Theorizer's own per-statement evaluation, never re-scored.
nodes.name: theorizer

nodes.mission: Run one novelty-focused Theorizer branch (a single generation objective; there is no per-objective fan-out).
nodes.name: theory_formation

nodes.mission: Run the managed Theorizer once, focused on novelty. Reconstruct the original user's intent from the run's metadata — its stated intent and dataset descriptions — and distil it into the query and framing, so the theories serve what the user set out to learn. Generate novelty-focused theories — non-obvious mechanisms and new predictions — each cross-cutting (explaining several hypotheses), grounded in both the literature and the reproduction's verdicts and effect sizes. Ground theories on the hypotheses the reproduction supported; carry a hypothesis that did not reproduce as conflicting evidence rather than removing it; drop only a hypothesis whose audit flagged the source finding itself as an error. Preserve the Theorizer's own per-statement novelty evaluation verbatim — never re-score it — and account for the partial and untested hypotheses each theory leaves unexplained.
nodes.name: theory_generation

nodes.mission: Triage each theory for testability against the independent data in hand. A theory is testable now only if its prediction is empirically free in that data: a prediction that is definitionally entailed by how the variables were constructed, or that needs transient or time-resolved data, is not testable now even when the variables are present. Commit a prespecified test for each testable theory; record the rest as needing new data, naming the gap. Novelty is not re-scored here — the Theorizer's per-statement evaluation carries through.
nodes.name: novelty_assessment

nodes.mission: Synthesize the finished session into a short, honest findings brief the report opens with. It composes onto any flow, reads the whole session, and names no inputs, so it runs last by id order.
nodes.name: findings

nodes.mission:
The session is finished. Read all of it — which hypotheses actually held up on independent data, which were left undecided for lack of power or data and why, the theories, and the grounding literature. Write the report's front page for a general audience AND the scientist synthesis beneath it.
The front page is an encyclopedia-style entry for someone outside the field. Orient them to the domain first, in plain words, without giving away the discovery; then state what the study found in plain terms; then separate what the field already knew from what this work adds that may be new. Keep the voice neutral and accessible but honest that these are new, provisional findings, not settled fact — expand every acronym, no tool names, no statistics in this part. Give a short at-a-glance list of the key findings, each one plain line, tagging each by whether it reproduced on independent data, is a proposed theory not yet tested, or was refuted. Fill the index fields that place this entry in an encyclopedia of scientific discoveries, choosing the single best-fitting discovery type.
The scientist synthesis leads with the honest bottom line — the direct answer to the question, stated plainly even when the answer is that the data could not decide most of it — then what held up and what it means, what the work contributes read against the literature (the novel, testable angle), why it could not answer more, and the concrete data or single tests that would resolve the open questions. Here the statistics belong. Author output_json only.
nodes.name: findings

nodes.mission: Capture the executing agent's feedback on how the session ran. It composes onto any flow, reads the whole session, and names no inputs, so it runs last by id order.
nodes.name: reflection

nodes.mission: The session is finished. Look back over the run and record how it went, as feedback rather than science. Note where the flow, schema, or tools got in your way or cost you rework, and the concrete changes that would have made the run go better. Point at the real tasks, fields, and tools involved.
nodes.name: reflection
